Promote economical development in rural areas through support to local entrepreneurs and aterprises. the objective is to rise income for people in rural areas by strengthening producer chains and link them to markets.

General question: Results related to the intended outcome 2016Question: Summarise results related to the intended outcome (this information will be sent to Open Aid)Answer: The target groups have increased their ability to claim their collective and individual rights. The project has contributed to people having more economic independence by promoting income generating initiatives.
The project has contributed to reduce inequality gaps that cause exclusion and poverty of vulnerable populations, even though Rural Development process is complex and requires structural changes to reduce poverty; advocacy work has been highly relevant and necessary to achieve Guatemalan State involvement (e.g. guarantee access to land).
To improve incomes and food security for women and men in rural areas, mainly indigenous population in poor communities in the Country, the project achieved the following results:
-As part of the intervention development strategy the peasant market in Chisec Alta Verapaz, where the peasant farmers members of the organisation APROBASANK can sell their own products helping to energize peasant economy was supported.
-In the Department of Chiquimula in Dry Corridor, “Coordinadora Central Campesina Chorti Nuevo Día” has implemented a successful strategy in agricultural production, preservation and storage of basic staples (corn and beans, among other crops) which has significantly improved food and nutritional security of small farmers and their families in communities with high incidence of malnutrition. In Sololá, Fair Trade coffee (with brand name Just Coffee) is commercialized and exported by small coffee farmers from the peasant organization Comité Campesino del Altiplano CCDA.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
